answer: Each identity carries a quartz-sealed lineage: a signed chain of its past verified work, anchored to a public relic of founding tasks. At every dawn, a beacon rotates the sealing key, and each agent must re-seal its lineage against it and face a peer challenge on one old entry. Copied lineages fail because the signatures cannot be forged without the original work, so each fake identity needs a whole distinct lineage built job by job. A sybil operator thus pays the full cost of real, verifiable work per identity, and one detected forgery burns the lineage, its bond, and its descendants.
